extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners handling PCT Chapter II Demands
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing a Demand for international preliminary examination under PCT Chapter II, and for making and processing Article 19/34 amendments, fees, translations, and related formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Demand shall be made on a standardized form (PCT Rule 53).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Demand should be filed on Form PCT/IPEA/401 along with the fee calculation sheet; printed forms are available from the USPTO (mark requests 'Mail Stop PCT') and forms are available on WIPO’s website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal refund rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of a proper Demand prior to the start of the international preliminary examination will entitle applicant to a refund of the preliminary examination fee minus the amount of the transmittal fee set forth in § 1.445(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Demand constitutes election
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a Demand shall constitute the election of all Contracting States which are designated and are bound by Chapter II of the Treaty on the international filing date (PCT Rule 53.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Demands filed before Jan 1, 2004, only those eligible states indicated as being elected are elected. Only PCT member states that have ratified/acceded to Chapter II and were designated in the Request may be elected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late Demand is ineffective
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Demand filed after the expiration of the applicable time limit set forth in PCT Rule 54 bis.1(a) shall be considered as if it had not been submitted (PCT Rule 54 bis.1(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file before the later of (A) three months from transmittal of the international search report and written opinion, or (B) 22 months from priority date; otherwise the Demand will be treated as not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend before IPEA report
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Article 34(2)(b), the applicant shall have a right to amend the claims, the description, and the drawings, in the prescribed manner and within the prescribed time limit, before the international preliminary examination report is established. The amendment shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may be filed with the Demand, within the period for reply to the written opinion of the ISA, or within the period for reply to the written opinion of the IPEA. See MPEP §§ 1871, 1878.02 for processing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of amendments — replacement sheets and letter
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending the description or the drawings, the applicant shall be required to submit a replacement sheet for every sheet which, on account of an amendment, differs from the sheet previously filed (PCT Rule 66.8(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheets must be accompanied by a letter drawing attention to the differences, indicating the basis for the amendment in the application as filed, and preferably explaining the reasons. For examples of indicating basis see MPEP § 1853.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of amendments — minor changes and cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment consists in the deletion of passages or in minor alterations or additions, the replacement sheet may be a copy of the relevant sheet containing the alterations or additions, provided clarity and direct reproducibility are not adversely affected. If an amendment cancels an entire sheet, this may be communicated in a letter (PCT Rule 66.8(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of claim amendments — replacement of entire claims set
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending the claims, Rule 46.5 shall apply mutatis mutandis. The set of claims submitted under Rule 46.5 shall replace all the claims originally filed or previously amended under Articles 19 or 34 (PCT Rule 66.8(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete set of claims in replacement of the claims as originally filed (or previously amended under Article 19) must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application was not filed in the language of publication, any amendments under Article 34 and any accompanying letter must be in the language of publication. Where the international preliminary examination is carried out on the basis of a translation, any such amendments and letters must be in the language of that translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendments are filed in another language, a translation into the language in which the examination is carried out must also be furnished. If not in required language, IPEA will invite applicant to furnish them within a reasonable time; failure means the IPEA will not take such amendments into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make a Demand — residence/nationality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicant who is a resident or national of a Contracting State bound by Chapter II, and whose international application has been filed with the receiving Office of or acting for such State, may make a demand for international preliminary examination (PCT Article 31(2) and PCT Rule 54).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are multiple applicants, it is sufficient that at least one be a resident or national of a Contracting State bound by Chapter II. If applicant is not entitled to make a Demand, the Demand is considered not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: States that may be elected
rubrics_metrics.description: The Demand shall indicate the Contracting State(s) in which the applicant intends to use the results of the international preliminary examination (elected States). Election may relate only to Contracting States already designated under Article 4 and bound by Chapter II (PCT Article 31(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional Contracting States may be elected later. Applicants referred to in certain paragraphs may have restrictions on which states they may elect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent's right to act before IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agent entitled to practice before the receiving Office where the international application was filed may represent the applicant before the international authorities (PCT Article 49).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner questions an attorney/agent's right to practice before the IPEA, consult the USPTO roster of registered attorneys and agents; Form PCT/IPEA/410 may be used to ask the receiving Office whether the agent has the right to practice before that Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and competence of IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should submit the International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) they desire to prepare the International Preliminary Examination Report; IPEA/US will serve for U.S. residents/nationals under various conditions depending on who acted as ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. residents/nationals may choose other IPEAs (EPO, KIPO, IP Australia, ILPO, JPO, IPOS) subject to the ISA and each authority's restrictions and competency rules. Information on demand filing with specific IPEA is on WIPO’s Applicant's Guide website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred filing methods and address rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Demands filed in the USPTO should preferably be filed via the USPTO patent electronic filing system by registered users; non-registered filers must file by another acceptable method. Do not file a courtesy copy with the USPTO if unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mailed to the USPTO use 'Mail Stop PCT' or hand-deliver per MPEP § 501. Priority Mail Express provisions may be used but failure to comply results in date-of-receipt not date-of-deposit. Certificate of Mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 cannot be used if deposit date is desired. Demands may be submitted via facsimile; see MPEP §§ 513, 1834, and 1834.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding when IPEA not competent (PCT Rule 59.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Demand is filed with an IPEA not competent for the particular international application, the USPTO will forward the Demand to the International Bureau, which will forward it to a competent IPEA. The competent IPEA will process the Demand based on the date of receipt in the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination and handling fees — payment timing and late fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The handling and preliminary examination fees shall be paid within the time period set in PCT Rule 57.3; the fee payable is the fee in effect on the date of payment (37 CFR 1.481). If fees are not paid within the time period, applicant will be notified and given one month to pay the deficient fees plus a late payment fee equal to the greater of: (i) 50% of deficient fees (not exceeding double the handling fee), or (ii) the handling fee (PCT Rule 58 bis.2). The one-month time limit may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required payment is not made the Demand will be declared as if not submitted. If payment is received on the same date the notification is sent, the fee is considered late and the notification remains effective. The preliminary examination fee may be higher if the international search was performed by an authority other than the USPTO. Current amounts found in Official Gazette and 37 CFR 1.482.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of defects in the Demand (PCT Rule 60)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Demand does not comply with specified requirements (Rules 53.1, 53.2(a)(i)-(iii), 53.2(b), 53.3-53.8 and 55.1), the IPEA shall invite the applicant to correct defects within a reasonable time limit, not less than one month. If corrected within the time limit, the Demand is considered as received on the actual filing date provided it permitted identification of the international application; otherwise the Demand is considered not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special provisions (a-bis, a-ter) govern multi-applicant indications and signatures. If defect noticed by IB, IB brings it to IPEA's attention. If Demand lacks a statement concerning amendments, IPEA proceeds as provided in Rules 66.1 and 69.1(a) or (b). If statement indicates amendments but none are submitted, IPEA will invite submission within fixed time and proceed per Rule 69.1(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of election to International Bureau and elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA shall promptly notify the International Bureau and the applicant of the filing of any Demand; the International Bureau notifies each elected Office of their election and notifies the applicant that such notification has been made (PCT Rule 61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document and translation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA needs a copy of the earlier application whose priority is claimed, the IB shall furnish such copy on request. If the copy is not furnished because applicant failed to comply with Rule 17.1, or the priority document is not available, the international preliminary examination report may be established as if the priority had not been claimed (PCT Rule 66.7(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier application is in a language other than a language of the IPEA and the validity of the priority claim is relevant, the IPEA may invite the applicant to furnish a translation within two months; failure allows establishment of the report as if priority not claimed. The IB may translate the priority document into English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission and treatment of Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a Demand the International Bureau shall promptly transmit to the IPEA a copy of the written opinion of the ISA and any amendment under Article 19 and any statement and the letter required under Rule 46.5(b), unless the Authority indicates it already received them (PCT Rule 62.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Article 19 amendments are filed after the Demand, applicant should preferably file a copy with the IPEA at same time. The IB marks replacement sheets received under Article 19 'AMENDED SHEET (ARTICLE 19)'. If an unstamped copy is received by IPEA/US, it will treat it as an Article 34 amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA start conditions for international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA starts the international preliminary examination when it is in possession of the demand; the required fees; required translations (if any); either the international search report or notice that no ISR will be established; and the written opinion established under Rule 43 bis.1, unless the applicant requests postponement until the later of three months from transmittal of the ISR/written opinion or 22 months from priority date (PCT Rule 62 and related text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions allow earlier start (A) if competent IPEA is same organization as ISA, (B) where statement indicates Article 19 amendments are to be taken into account (IPEA waits to receive them), (C) where statement requests postponement (IPEA waits for copies or notice or specified time), and (D) other special circumstances described in PCT Rule 53.9.
